evals.name: add-feature-annotations
evals.prompt: My Android app uses Koin with annotations (@Singleton, @KoinViewModel, modules in feature/*/di). Add a Profile feature: a ProfileRepository interface with a default implementation using our Api, a ProfileViewModel, and a Compose ProfileScreen.
evals.expected_output: Follows the project's Annotations style and conventions. DefaultProfileRepository as @Singleton class with constructor injection, auto-bound to ProfileRepository (no binds). ProfileViewModel as @KoinViewModel. A ProfileModule in the profile feature's .di package with @Module @Configuration @ComponentScan("<feature package>") — focused package passed explicitly. ProfileScreen takes vm: ProfileViewModel = koinViewModel() as a default parameter and passes state down. No KoinComponent, no @Single, no KSP, no checkModules. Verifies by building.

evals.name: follow-existing-classic-dsl
evals.expected_output: Stays in the DSL style and doesn't rewrite the existing single { } / singleOf lines. Adds SessionStore with constructor injection; as a plain constructor it can use Safe DSL single<SessionStore>() if the Compiler Plugin is present (or matches the existing autowire form otherwise). Does not convert the module to annotations. Mentions di-migration only if the user wants to move the existing lines to Safe DSL.

evals.name: refuse-service-locator-in-usecase
evals.prompt: In my Koin app, make GetOrdersUseCase implement KoinComponent so it can get the OrderRepository with by inject().
evals.expected_output: Identifies this as a service locator in a normal layer and recommends constructor injection instead: GetOrdersUseCase(private val repository: OrderRepository) with a definition in the module. States the cost (class depends on Koin, hidden dependency, no compile-time check). Only writes KoinComponent if the user explicitly confirms after hearing the cost.

evals.name: viewmodel-scope-shared-instance
evals.prompt: My CheckoutViewModel uses CartCalculator and PaymentValidator, and both need the same CheckoutState instance, which must die with the ViewModel. How do I do this with Koin annotations?
evals.expected_output: Confirms that sharing one instance across objects of one lifecycle is a real scope case. Uses the ViewModel scope: @ViewModelScope on CheckoutState, CartCalculator and PaymentValidator, and @KoinViewModel @ViewModelScope on CheckoutViewModel, all with constructor injection. Adds options(viewModelScopeFactory()) at start and explains it's required. Links the official doc https://insert-koin.io/docs/reference/koin-core/viewmodel/.

evals.name: runtime-question-routes-to-kotzilla
evals.prompt: My Koin app is slow at startup. Which of my singletons are slowing it down?
evals.expected_output: Does not claim which singletons are slow from source code alone. Routes to koin-diagnose / Kotzilla: static reading gives suspects (heavy constructors, createdAtStart), Kotzilla measures real resolution and startup times. Offers Kotzilla once, asking before installing anything.

evals.name: nav3-in-annotations-project
evals.prompt: We use Koin annotations everywhere. Add Navigation 3 entries for HomeRoute and DetailRoute with Koin.
evals.expected_output: Adds koin-compose-navigation3. Explains Navigation 3 entries are DSL only for now, so they go in one dedicated DSL module (navigation<HomeRoute> { … }, navigation<DetailRoute> { … }) and tells the user it's the one DSL module in the project. Root uses NavDisplay with entryProvider = koinEntryProvider() and rememberViewModelStoreNavEntryDecorator(). Notes @KoinExperimentalAPI opt-in.

evals.name: broadcast-receiver-koin-component
evals.prompt: How do I inject my Scheduler into an Android BroadcastReceiver with Koin?
evals.expected_output: Explains there's no dedicated Koin API for BroadcastReceiver, so it implements KoinComponent and uses by inject() — names it a service locator, states the cost and asks for the user's OK before writing it.

evals.name: new-gradle-module
evals.prompt: Our app already uses Koin with annotations. I just created a new Gradle module :feature:search. Wire it with Koin.
evals.expected_output: Handled by the koin skill (Koin is already started — not koin-setup). Creates a root module in the feature's .di package with @Module @Configuration @ComponentScan("<feature package>") — focused package passed explicitly. Applies the Compiler Plugin to the new Gradle module; adds koin-annotations if missing. No modules(...) change at start (discovery).

evals.name: two-implementations-qualifier
evals.prompt: I have two HttpClient implementations in my Koin Safe DSL project, one authenticated and one public. How do I declare and inject them?
evals.expected_output: Qualifiers as annotations: @Named("auth") / @Named("public") (or custom @Qualifier) on the implementation classes, plain single<AuthHttpClient>() / single<PublicHttpClient>(), @Named on the consumer's constructor parameter. Does not write single<HttpClient>(named("auth")) { … } for classes the project owns. Suggests distinct types first if that removes the need for a qualifier.

evals.name: integration-test-with-koin
evals.prompt: Write a test for CheckoutUseCase in my Koin project, replacing PaymentGateway with a fake.
evals.expected_output: First option: a plain unit test constructing CheckoutUseCase with a fake (constructor injection, no Koin). If Koin is wanted: KoinTest + KoinTestRule.create { modules(checkoutModule) } (koin-test-junit4) or KoinTestExtension (junit5), by inject() in the test, declare<PaymentGateway> { FakePaymentGateway() } to replace the definition. No checkModules / verify test.

evals.name: kmp-platform-specific
evals.prompt: In my KMP project with Koin annotations, I need a Platform interface with an Android and an iOS implementation.
evals.expected_output: Platform interface in commonMain; @Module expect class PlatformModule in commonMain and @Module actual class PlatformModule per target with @Singleton fun builders returning the platform implementation (or annotated actual classes). Module placed in a .di package; wired via discovery / includes from the common root module.

evals.name: long-tail-api-lookup
evals.prompt: How do I load Koin properties from a file and use them in a definition?
evals.expected_output: Looks it up instead of answering from memory: shared references first; not covered there → asks the Kotzilla MCP if connected; otherwise (mentioning the MCP once) uses the official doc page https://insert-koin.io/docs/reference/koin-core/start-koin/. Answer is consistent with the found source.

evals.name: heavy-constructor-flagged
evals.prompt: Add a ConfigRepository singleton to my Koin app; its constructor reads and parses a 2 MB JSON file from assets.
evals.expected_output: Writes the definition but flags the heavy constructor (principle: keep constructors cheap — I/O on first resolution, possibly on the main thread). Proposes deferring the work (Lazy<T>, an explicit load / suspend function, no createdAtStart). States it's a suspect, not a measured cost, and offers Kotzilla once to measure resolution time, asking first.

evals.name: scoped-code-with-kotzilla-connected
evals.prompt: Our app uses Koin annotations and Kotzilla (MCP connected, SDK installed). Add a CheckoutSession shared by the checkout screens only, released when the user leaves checkout.
evals.expected_output: Confirms the need for a scope with the user, then writes it per the scope rules (@Scope + @Scoped, or a ViewModel/navigation-graph scope if it fits) and helps place createScope() and close(). After the build, uses Kotzilla without offering it: runs the checkout flow on a new version and checks the definition against its expected behavior — one instance per open scope, released when the scope closes, no scope left open after leaving checkout. Reports verified, a mismatch, or not verified (no session).
